findings.title: The planar chromatic minimum is misstated
findings.claim: The minimum possible chromatic number of a planar norm's unit-distance graph is two.
findings.hypotheses: Any norm on R^2; no genericity or strict convexity assumption is needed for the refutation.
findings.decisive_evidence: For every planar norm take a continuous unit-circle arc from x to -x. The distance to x varies continuously from 0 to 2, so a point y on the arc has ||y-x||=1. Then 0,x,y are distinct and pairwise unit separated, giving a triangle. Thus no planar norm's unit-distance graph is bipartite.
findings.counterinterpretations: A single Euclidean triangle would not refute the minimum over all norms; the argument is universal. It does not supply a contradiction to the correctly stated typical value four.
findings.impact: False concluding local statement. Theorem 1.4 and its Section 6 proof use four correctly; no principal theorem damage established.
findings.repair: Replace two by four, using the manuscript's cited universal lower bound four and its typical upper bound. The independent triangle argument alone proves only the lower bound three, which suffices to refute two.
findings.repair_limits: The Chilakamarri universal lower-bound proof remains an external dependency, not independently reproduced.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: The concluding assertion is a minimum over every planar norm. The refutation must therefore apply to every norm, including nonsmooth and non-strictly-convex unit balls.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For a Euclidean unit semicircle v(t) from v to -v, gamma(t)=v(t)/||v(t)|| is a continuous arc of the norm unit circle. Set x=gamma(0). The continuous function ||gamma(t)-x|| has endpoint values 0 and 2. The intermediate value theorem gives y with ||y-x||=1; 0,x,y are distinct and pairwise at norm distance one. Thus every such unit graph contains a triangle. This proves a universal lower bound three and rules out the printed two.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: A Euclidean example alone would not settle a minimum over norms. The manuscript itself gives four in Theorem 1.4 and cites the universal lower bound four earlier, so the wrong sentence does not contradict the correctly scoped typical-norm theorem.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: Local concluding misstatement; the Section 6 coloring proof and Theorem 1.4 use four. No principal theorem failure is established.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Replace two by four using the manuscript's cited universal lower bound plus its typical upper bound. The independent triangle argument supplies only >=3, not a fresh proof of Chilakamarri's >=4 theorem.

findings.title: The collinear dichotomy omits a boundary/interior pair
findings.claim: Distinct collinear a,b in the unit ball either have max(||a||,||b||)<1 or a=-b.
findings.hypotheses: Distinct nonzero collinear points in a norm unit ball; choose the Euclidean unit disk.
findings.decisive_evidence: a=(1,0), b=(1/2,0) are distinct, collinear and in the Euclidean unit disk, have maximum norm one and are not antipodal. Their midpoint has norm 3/4, so the desired strict-convexity conclusion survives.
findings.calculation: independent_checks.py uses exact Fraction values and verifies maximum norm one, non-antipodality, and midpoint norm 3/4.
findings.impact: False local explanatory dichotomy; no loss of the strict-convexity criterion or later geometric approximation established.
findings.repair: Replace max by min. If either norm is below one the convex-combination bound is strict; if both equal one distinct collinear points are antipodal, giving |2 alpha-1|<1.
findings.repair_limits: No new strict-convexity hypothesis or altered main conclusion is needed.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: Distinct nonzero collinear a,b in a norm unit ball and 0<alpha<1. The Euclidean disk is an admissible instance, including the case of one boundary and one interior point.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Take a=(1,0), b=(1/2,0). The maximum norm is one, and a is not -b; hence the printed dichotomy is false. The desired midpoint still has norm 3/4. More generally, if min(||a||,||b||)<1, the convex-combination norm is <1 by the triangle inequality with two positive weights. If both norms equal one, distinct collinear unit vectors are antipodal, giving |2alpha-1|<1.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: Neither the counterexample nor the repair invalidates the strict-convexity criterion. Zero-vector cases are already handled separately by the manuscript.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: A local omitted boundary/interior case in the explanatory proof, not a failure of the criterion or later approximation arguments.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Use min in place of max. All collinear cases and endpoint restrictions are then covered without new hypotheses.

findings.title: Missing one-half factor in the entropy induction display

location.anchor: Final display in the proof of Lemma 4.4

findings.claim: The printed middle expression subtracts the full sum of ni log2(ni) for i=2,...,ell-1.
findings.hypotheses: Positive sorted integer parts. Take ell=3 and n1=n2=n3=2, n=6, n1'=4.
findings.decisive_evidence: The three printed quantities are -1, -2, and 6-3 log2(6). The second inequality is false because -2<6-3 log2(6), equivalent to 216<256.
findings.calculation: Exact integer countercomparison in independent_checks.py; 7337 integer partitions of n<=24 also checked against the correctly stated lemma by integer exponentiation.
findings.impact: The intermediate display is false. The preceding binary-entropy computation supplies the correct half-weighted remainder, and the subsequent forest proof uses the correct lemma. No substantive loss of the general argument is identified.
findings.repair: Insert 1/2 before the remaining sum. The preceding two-variable estimate and induction then give the corrected two-step inequality for every admissible partition.
findings.repair_limits: The finite partition diagnostic is not the proof for all n; the analytic entropy induction is the general repair.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: Sorted positive integer parts with ell>=1; the witness (2,2,2) satisfies every hypothesis.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: At (2,2,2), n=6 and n1'=4, the printed chain is -1 >= -2 >= 6-3log2(6). The second comparison is false: 6-3log2(6)>-2 is equivalent to 6^3<2^8, namely 216<256. For all admissible parts, set t=n1/(n1+nell) in [1/2,1]. Concavity gives H(t)>=2-2t, so n1-1/2[n1log n1+nell log nell] >= n1'-1/2 n1'log n1'. Subtract the remaining half-weighted terms and apply induction to the still sorted parts n1',n2,...,nell-1. This proves the corrected chain generally.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: The general two-part entropy calculation immediately above the false display is already correct, as is the lemma and its subsequent use in the forest argument. Finite enumeration of 7337 partitions is supporting historical computation, not the proof for all n.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: Minor transcription defect in an intermediate display. The rating rests on the existing correct general argument and correct downstream use, not merely on how short the repair is.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Insert 1/2 before the remaining sum. No change to Lemma 4.4 or the main combinatorial estimate is required.
